subject: e2e console guard is stricter (fixtures.ts, 4609a60): failed requests of the app's own page now fail tests
body:
From 4609a60 the consoleErrors fixture works as follows:
- 'Failed to load resource' lines are never ignored, whatever origin they are attributed to.
- Failed requests are judged by frame. Every main-frame response >= 400 and every main-frame requestfailed is an error. Excepted: cancelled requests, deliberately offline ones, and service-worker requests (they have no frame).
- Other console lines are ignored only when they come from the YouTube/Google embed hosts (youtube-nocookie.com, youtube.com, google.com, gstatic.com).
- Expected failures still go through consoleErrors.allowHttpError({urlPart, status}). Use status 0 for a request that fails without a response, e.g. one your test aborts with page.route.
Why: the previous fromNonAppFrame hid a broken cross-origin image or fetch of the app's page (the Supabase gateway on localhost, Commons, PMC). console-guard.spec.ts proves the new behaviour.
What you may see: a spec that passed before can now fail with 'failed requests of the app's own page' listing the URL. That is a real error your page made, or one your test should declare with allowHttpError. Firefox newly reports fetch 4xx that it never printed to the console.
Sandbox note: behind the agent TLS proxy, Firefox rejects third-party HTTPS (SEC_ERROR_UNKNOWN_ISSUER). If your spec loads Commons/PMC/YouTube in Firefox locally, opt in with E2E_IGNORE_HTTPS_ERRORS=1 the way agent.spec does. CI has no proxy.
